name: Mephibosheth
overview: Mephibosheth was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, uniquely identified as a son of Saul. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional personal notes or background about him. His role is noted specifically in 2 Samuel 21:8.
namesAndTitles: The name Mephibosheth means 'from the mouth of Shame,' which is a derogatory reference to Baal. This proper name was not given by God but is recorded in 2 Samuel 21:8, reflecting the cultural and religious context of his time.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Mephibosheth as a son of Saul and Rizpah, establishing his direct lineage within Saul's family. No other family relationships are documented beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Mephibosheth's significance lies in his identity as a son of Saul, linking him to the first king of Israel and the complex legacy of Saul's house. His mention in 2 Samuel 21:8 situates him within the broader narrative of Saul's descendants and the unfolding history of Israel. Although details are sparse, his presence underscores the continuing relevance of Saul's lineage in biblical history.
